qa.teardown_note: MANUAL, surgical teardown — deliberately NOT qa-complete's down.sh drop path. This worktree used the SHARED LITERAL clarity/zod ClickHouse databases (the repo hardcodes those names in ~15 query classes), and the same container also hosts clarity_claude_dev_2409 and clarity_claude_dev_2426. Dropping the databases or stopping the container would have broken two other worktrees. Done: deleted only the seeded rows (org 5 from kit_scan_paths, qa-* mappings from sc_positions — both verified 0 remaining); dropped the two provably per-worktree Postgres DBs behind a name guard (shared zod/zod_testing verified intact); restored MAIL_MAILER=smtp; unlinked the per-worktree Herd site (6 other worktree sites verified still linked); deleted the ledger. NOT restored: CLICKHOUSE_HOST to Cloud — the original readonly_user password was replaced in Phase 4 and is not recoverable from the ledger, so restoring the host alone would leave a broken half-config; and the pipeline's own rule is never to wire Cloud into a worktree. Left pointing at the local container, which is both safe and the documented preference.

h1_all_three_lanes.claim: The tier-2 point budget is far too large to prevent the OOM it was added to prevent; the guard admits selections that will fatal.
h1_all_three_lanes.lane_evidence: okf/concepts/platform-gotchas.md:166 (PG-022) ~1.5 KB/point vs a 256M web memory_limit; docs/investigations/DEV-2177/state.json measured 1,509 bytes/point and set MAX_RENDER_POINTS ~= 120K for 'exactly this shape'. Lanes concluded the budget is ~12x too large.
h1_all_three_lanes.driver_verdict: CONCLUSION CONFIRMED, MAGNITUDE WRONG — and the driver's own earlier figure was also wrong.
h1_all_three_lanes.driver_measurement: Measured through the ACTUAL KitScanPathsQuery + real ClickHouse driver by seeding local CH (not a synthetic benchmark, and not an extrapolation from either side): 120K pts -> 34.8 MB, 255K -> 76.3 MB, 502.5K -> 156.2 MB, 630K -> 195.4 MB. Linear at ~325 bytes/point. Laravel baseline peak is 79 MB, so usable payload headroom under a 256M limit is ~177 MB => a hard ceiling of ~545K points.
h1_all_three_lanes.why_the_lane_number_is_wrong: PG-022's ~1.5 KB/point is explicitly the cost of 'inflating each GPS point into a keyed PHP array FOR HistoricPathBuilder'. Tier 2 never touches HistoricPathBuilder — kit_scan_paths returns pre-bucketed path_points tuple arrays that are json_encode'd directly. The lanes applied a constant measured on a different code shape.
h1_all_three_lanes.why_the_driver_number_was_also_wrong: An earlier synthetic PHP benchmark gave ~258 bytes/point because it never modelled the ClickHouse driver, which buffers the whole response as a string and then json_decode()s it. That was proven when a 500K-point run OOM'd at 128M INSIDE the driver's json_decode, before any row-building code ran. Measuring the real path was the only way to settle it.

consequences.budget_as_set_1_500_000: 1.5M x 325 B = ~488 MB + 79 MB baseline = ~567 MB => ~2.2x over a 256M limit. The lanes are right that it admits fatal selections. Root cause of the driver's error: MAX_RENDER_POINTS was RAISED to 1.5M precisely BECAUSE tier 1 stopped materializing points (its docblock says so); reusing it for the tier that still does materialize them inverts the reason it was raised.
consequences.org_469_8_kits_30d_423375_pts: ~138 MB + 79 = ~217 MB — fits under 256M but with only ~39 MB headroom.

options.A_tier2_specific_budget: ~500K points. Passes org 469's reported case at every date range, refuses All Kits and the worst org. Small diff. Cost: only ~39 MB headroom on the passing case — 'thinner than comfortable', the same words DEV-2177's own note used about its budget.
options.B_preencode_in_clickhouse: What PG-022 actually prescribes: 'take PHP out of the per-point path entirely: segment inside ClickHouse and return each path pre-encoded (toJSONString), so cost becomes O(segments)'. KitRangePathsQuery is the worked example — 7 days x all kits for a 200-kit org went from ~1 GB (refused) to ~20 MB / 3,491 segments. Removes the ceiling instead of drawing a tight line under it.

Org 469 'All Kits' + 30d = 1,638,423 tier-2 points > 1.5M, so a selection that previously returned 200 with kit 15349's route returned 422 with an empty map. converged_finding_fixed.resolution: FIXED (operator decision): over-budget now degrades to tier-1-only with 200 and a logged warning; 422 is reserved for when tier 1 has nothing to show either. Restructured the shared-budget test to assert 200 + tier-1-only (it still pins sharedness — a per-tier budget would have admitted the scan-only kit) and added test_over_budget_with_no_tier_one_rows_still_returns_422. Mutation-verified: restoring the unconditional 422 fails exactly the new test.

recorded_not_fixed.finding: The budget bounds POINTS but tier 2 allocates per BUCKET. At 2 points/bucket, 1.5M points would admit 750,000 rows at ~350-400 B each plus path_json plus the row string, roughly 400-500 MB — about 2x the limit — while the counter reads only 1.5M. Does not materialise today: the fleet's largest per-org bucket count is 55,447 (~55 MB of row overhead vs a 256 MB limit, ~10x margin) and org 469 runs ~68 points/bucket. claude3's framing is fair and worth preserving: the envelope is safe by an accident of current bucket density, not by construction. Cheap hardening if it ever matters: also refuse on bucket count, or divide the point budget by an assumed minimum points-per-bucket.
